display_name: Jupiter ruler of the 1st House in the 1st House
description: You walk into rooms as the wise one — the principled, expansive, slightly larger-than-life self. In love, that is both gift and friction: partners are drawn to the gravity, then sometimes feel they must enroll in your school. You need a counterpart who is your peer in conviction, who can challenge a principle without flinching. Relationships fail when you turn intimacy into doctrine; they thrive when you let your partner correct you out of their own equal authority.

display_name: Jupiter ruler of the 4th House in the 1st House
description: Home is co-extensive with your person — you carry your foundation in your body. Mother is not a distant figure but a wisdom-anchor who shaped your sense of self. The dwelling reads as an extension of who you are. Relationships compound when partners can integrate into the home you already are; they fail when partners ask you to dismantle the foundation to fit them in.

display_name: Mercury ruler of the 10th House in the 10th House
description: Public-facing relationship-as-brand is at peak articulation. The world reads you and your partner as a precision unit; reputation is shared and carefully composed. Joint announcements, joint career-moves, joint public-statements all carry weight. The shadow: marrying the joint press release rather than the partner — verify the relationship works at home, not only on the public stage.

display_name: Mercury ruler of the 7th House in the 10th House
description: Marriage and primary partnership lean public, professional, peer-aged or peer-status. The spouse is met through career or formal channels and the relationship is part of your public face from the start. Industries: a partner who is a peer-professional; a deal-attorney; a co-founder. The relationship is also the brand. The shadow: confusing the joint career with the joint heart — the resume-quality of the union doesn't guarantee the home-quality; verify both.

display_name: Venus ruler of the 11th House in the 11th House
description: Friendships, social networks, and elder-friend circles are sovereign — and feminine, aesthetic, diplomatic in tone. Senior female mentors function as second-mothers across decades. Romantic introductions arrive through the female-led friend network. Group friendships rather than tight pairs are the primary social structure. The shadow: a friend-circle so warm and large that it dilutes the primary partnership — protect couple-time from network gravity.

display_name: Venus ruler of the 6th House in the 11th House
description: In intimate-circle conflicts you negotiate gracefully through the friend-network. Old workplace tensions resolve through the senior-female ally; the difficult sibling-conversation gets routed through a mutual friend. Friend-circle and conflict-zone overlap in your life — the people you fight with often become the people you befriend. The shadow: keeping problematic friends because the gain channel is real; clean the boundary even at gain-cost.

display_name: Saturn ruler of the 2nd House in the 2nd House
description: Speech of love runs slow, structural, and final. You don't flirt easily; you don't say "I love you" until you mean it for decades. Family-finance with the partner is approached with care: the joint account, the inheritance question, the long savings ritual. The voice that says affection prefers commitment-language to performance-language. The shadow: under-spoken affection that the partner reads as coldness — your slow words are deeper, but make sure they actually arrive.

display_name: Saturn ruler of the 3rd House in the 2nd House
description: Communication with siblings, peers, and close friends is methodical, structural, and a touch formal. You write rather than call; you prepare rather than improvise. Younger siblings or cohort-mates often look to you as the steady one. The shadow: peer-friendship that feels more like a project than a play — schedule unstructured time with the close ones; warmth needs space to wander.

display_name: Mars ruler of the 12th House in the 5th House
description: Bedroom-pleasures, hidden romance, and behind-the-scenes intimacy carry sharp, decisive, body-anchored charge that gets expressed through creative-public output. The book inspired by the love affair, the project incubated during the foreign trip with the partner, the speculative bet placed in retreat — these are how the 12H sweet-pleasure becomes the 5H visible win. The shadow: pleasure-spending on travel that drains the speculative budget; honor the foreign romance, but discipline the cost.

display_name: Mars ruler of the 5th House in the 5th House
description: Romance runs sharp, decisive, body-anchored, and pulled toward action rather than rumination. You like the partner who can keep up with the speed; you choose people who do not need lengthy reassurance to make moves. Children, mentees, and creative work are the visible love-objects. The shadow: speed in commitment that outruns due diligence — slow down enough to verify character, even when the chemistry says go.

display_name: Moon ruler of the 8th House in the 8th House
description: Sexuality, deep intimacy, and shared resources have an emotional fluency in the depths that few partners can match. You are not afraid of hard conversations about money, mortality, in-laws, inheritance. You bring genuine emotional depth to the parts of the relationship that most couples avoid. The shadow: drawing partners into emotional storms because the depth-charge is what feels real — learn to inhabit calm intimacy too, not only the dark-water dives.

display_name: Sun ruler of the 9th House in the 9th House
description: Romance is filtered through values, ethics, philosophy, foreign-fortune, and shared worldview — and the supreme dharma engine of the chart makes this lens stronger than usual. You commit to people whose principles you respect, lose interest fast in those whose ethics blur, and find foreign or cross-cultural partnerships natural. Teacher-student dynamics, age-gap relationships, pilgrimage-style courtships are all native. The shadow: principled rigidity that turns love into a doctrinal exam.
